newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India's Kandla oil jetties seen closed to 2H Nov.
newsitem.headline: India's Kandla oil jetties seen closed to 2H Nov.

text.p: The two floating jetties for oil products at the Indian west coast port of Kandla remained closed on Tuesday and were not expected to reopen until the second half of November, a Hindustan Petroleum Corp Ltd (HPCL) official said on Tuesday.
"We hope to be ready by end November," the HPCL official said. HPCL owns one jetty and state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) the other.
Shipping sources said the shutdown of the jetties has added three-to-five days to the previous one-to-two week queuing time for ships waiting to discharge oil cargoes.
The two jetties were closed on October 20-21 after a collision involving two tankers.
The official said repair work on HPCL's jetty would begin after the removal of one of the tanker's anchor and chain, which had entangled with the floating jetty.
"Between today and tomorrow...the anchors and chains will be retrieved," he said.
"The IOC jetty may start earlier but I am not sure. Maybe it will be back in 10 days," he said. IOC officials were not available for comment.
Kandla is India's biggest oil port and handled about 8 million tonnes of petroleum products and 12.5 million tonnes of crude last year.
The port's importance is enhanced by the 1,443 km Haldia-Batinda pipeline which transports petroleum products to north India.
As a result of the closure of the two jetties IOC has curbed its diesel and kerosene imports via Kandla port, traders said.
Of the 13 diesel cargoes purchased for December arrival totalling 520,000-tonnes, only four are to be delivered to the west coast ports of Goa or Kandla, they said.
Also, IOC has stopped taking diesel for delivery to nearby Vadinar port because of the longer time it takes to lighter tankers anchored off the port to Kandla for eventual shipment inland.
"The turnaround of daughter vessels has slowed down...(because) they are also sharing the main oil jetties. This has added to the congestion," one shipping source in Bombay told Reuters by telephone.
Large tankers anchor outside Vadinar and their cargoes are trans-shipped to Kandla using smaller barges.
Shipping sources said that of the 11 vessels waiting outside Kandla port, three are carrying diesel, compared to eight on October 25.
But the number of tankers in Vadinar waiting for discharge has not dropped significantly, they said. There are 11 diesel tankers waiting to discharge compared to 12 on October 25.
